claims: MTM-001 foundation and governance is completed with an accepted append-only receipt.
Rust 1.98.0 is pinned and the minimal workspace passes format, Clippy, tests, and golden contract checks.
MTM-002 is completed with Rust authoritative only for MTM-reboot's typed side-effect-free contract and policy core.
The frozen 135-case Python-Rust corpus has zero final mismatches and reference SHA-256 1aab731f737a00a9b40e614b7751e54d1418676febbb82cbc2e009dfc994430d.
MTM-003 is completed with Rust authoritative for MTM-reboot's independent Native process/isolation component while Re-CTM remains the deployed production runtime.
The normalized Native differential hash is 5c9e6b661d65d3442a42239018c5b0b8ca2bdd14d15947f604c4f8c625dc6f69 with zero final exact or lifecycle mismatches.

The current Linux target passed 14 implementation-hash-bound checks covering Bubblewrap, private-root denial, read-only toolchains, SageMath, Magma, helper parity, TTY, timeout/kill, and Quick Tunnel cleanup.
MTM-004 is completed with Rust authoritative inside MTM-reboot for schema-2 SQLite persistence, project/reference state, atomic promotion and capability signing plus registry validation.

The 52-operation Python-Rust state/capability corpus, physical database snapshots, v0/v1/v2 migrations, failure rollback and backup restoration all match reference SHA-256 bf0ecab52a25d2edc7fe47c95579a311dc7f14a2f1c4d2fd3e40b7f0d37d94f6.

The current Linux target passed ten redacted implementation-bound checks using a read-only online backup of the configured Re-CTM state database, exact rollback, cross-runtime capabilities and serialized writers.
MTM-005 is completed with Rust authoritative inside MTM-reboot for OAuth DCR/PKCE/code/token behavior, HTTP routing and Origin/CORS, legacy/modern MCP and exact public/hidden tool dispatch.
The 44-record Python-Rust gateway corpus has zero final mismatches and reference SHA-256 787e659b8787fab7765e2ae2bdb7ce774f2484467933fc87624097a9af65e849.

The ordered 24-tool public catalog hash is 86c8ee7d53a0678d0aaaba47ce2f2f72f5c03747fcb443d78011e005dedaa343 and all 35 public/hidden definitions hash to e89c5d2f8bec198fb4a90e7166aadb04b757e4b3ff0c8f459e5fdd468c59f87e.

The current Linux target passed fifteen implementation-hash-bound real gateway checks using Firefox, DCR/PKCE, single-use codes, exact catalogs, legacy/modern MCP, CORS/origin and fixed/dynamic issuer paths.

MTM-006 is completed with Rust authoritative inside MTM-reboot for workflow state, private vault, proof manifests/reference audits, server-computed verification, repair/escalation, mechanical finalization and project promotion.
The MTM-006 shadow corpus has 82 exact Python-Rust checkpoints with zero mismatches and reference SHA-256 def4f7abd3878638ff84952ce2632480eb427649a83868660087c97790de10b0.

The current Linux target passed eight implementation-and-harness-hash-bound pdflatex/finalization checks; all MTM-003 through MTM-006 target evidence was rerun after MTM-007 changed the shared lockfile.

CapabilityClaims cannot be publicly field-constructed or deserialized, and FinalizationPermit is crate-private with a verifier-private constructor; the vault re-hashes exact proof bytes before final publication.

A post-commit MTM-006 revalidation caught and repaired an all-targets build defect, an invalid real-pdflatex fixture, an unbound acceptance harness, and an overly broad crate-private permit constructor before the milestone was marked completed.

MTM-007 is completed with Rust authoritative inside MTM-reboot for the single runtime composition root, remaining file/Git/image/research/LaTeX adapters, real RuntimeToolBackend, CLI/TUI, Quick Tunnel composition and single-binary distribution.
The MTM-007 full-composition Python-Rust corpus has eighteen exact checkpoints with zero mismatches and frozen SHA-256 6aa4f5699df7099d29c12859788430bd6b1c66a8295828598b6cae62a964d830.

The embedded tool catalog decodes to frozen raw SHA-256 46deeeb246f77056c75392c2d14a3d707521c043fbead29b76bb5a44c6915dc3 and the methodology asset matches SHA-256 0403ba1f6caeabfef563e3b2b22bf1472a84c470a76ddbcb5bafce1d5f18a4e8.

The current Linux MTM-007 target passed twelve implementation-hash-bound release checks covering no-Python linkage, cargo-install distribution, Bubblewrap Native execution, real HTTPS research, real LaTeX/finalization, verified artifact delivery, TUI redaction, graceful SIGINT, Quick Tunnel public metadata/owned cleanup and A5 resource non-regression.

The final MTM-007 A5 workload recorded Python median/p95 160.101/160.888 ms with 29,992 KiB median RSS and Rust release median/p95 56.918/80.358 ms with 13,140 KiB median RSS; this is acceptance evidence only, not an A6 production-performance claim.

OAuthPrincipal is no longer publicly constructible/deserializable in production; the legacy shadow constructor is feature-gated off by default, and OperatorSession owns no storage/capability/vault/workflow authority.

MTM-008 began only after commit 5c7aa283977bc705f425efe23f6fcb0ac7a9359b, the MTM-007 golden, all lower target evidence and the complete local gate were revalidated; no production authority has moved yet.

The MTM-008 Rust 0.3.0 candidate is shadow-qualified: release identity and no-Python linkage, immutable Python-wheel restore, temporary atomic cutover/rollback/recutover, all prior target evidence, a sixty-second soak and bounded A6 qualification pass.

On the exact authenticated local OAuth/MCP mixed workload with eight clients, the latest accepted A6 run observed a 2.276x median throughput ratio, a 0.526 p95-latency ratio and a 0.669 peak-RSS ratio for Rust versus Python; this claim is limited to that recorded workload.
The current sixty-second Rust soak completed 167,122 requests with zero errors and 29 stateful start/cancel cycles, no file-descriptor or thread growth, no child process, and graceful shutdown.
Re-CTM remains the sole production authority.
No A6 performance improvement is claimed.
